identity.title: Generative Social Choice: The Next Generation

problem.claim: Generate a concise slate of statements that proportionally represents the spectrum of user opinions when possible statements are accessed only through specific queries.

gap.claim: The prior generative social choice framework did not address theoretical guarantees under approximately optimal queries together with an overall slate-length budget.

contributions.claim: Extends generative social choice with theoretical guarantees for approximately optimal queries and a bound on the slate’s total length.
Applies the approach to unstructured opinions about city improvement measures and drug reviews using GPT-4o queries.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their work by adding approximate-query guarantees and an overall slate-length budget to generative social choice.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report demonstrating effectiveness in generating representative slates from unstructured user opinions on city-improvement and drug-review datasets.
The authors report theoretical guarantees under approximately optimal queries and an overall slate-length budget.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames proportional representation of user opinions as producing a concise statement slate.
Unlike ordinary committee elections, the candidate space contains all possible variable-length statements and is query-accessed.
It situates the task within generative social choice, combining social choice with large language models.
It adds approximate-query and length-budget guarantees, then reports GPT-4o-based demonstrations on two opinion datasets.

source_observation.claim: The abstract states the task’s representation objective, unusual query-access model, theoretical constraints, and application domains.

lessons.interpretation: A compact abstract can make a contribution legible by aligning the task setting, the precise extension, and evidence contexts.
lessons.application: When presenting a new method, explicitly connect each claimed advance to the task constraint it addresses and name the datasets or domains used for demonstration.
lessons.exception: This structure is less suitable when the work is purely theoretical or has no concrete application setting to report.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the form of the theoretical guarantees, the query approximation assumptions, or the slate-length budget.
It does not provide quantitative results, baselines, dataset sizes, or details of the GPT-4o query implementation.
